newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China dissidents in HK safe after 1997 - Governor.
newsitem.headline: China dissidents in HK safe after 1997 - Governor.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Sunday Chinese dissidents living in the colony should be able to leave before it reverts to China next year while those intending to stay should not be threatened by Beijing.
Concern has been expressed for some 80 Chinese dissidents living in exile in Hong Kong with only eight months to go before the British colony is handed back to China next July 1.
"We understand the problem and we understand our responsibilities, and I hope there isn't a problem on the first of July next year," Patten told the government radio.

"Those who wish to leave should have been able to do so. As for the others, it's important to go on and on underlining the fact Hong Kong is promised that it will continue to be a free society. That lies at the heart of what China promised Hong Kong."
A 1984 Sino-British treaty pledges the territory considerable autonomy and the right to maintain capitalist freedoms for 50 years after it reverts to Chinese rule.
Patten said it was important for China to keep its promise.
"If Hong Kong becomes less free, it will be less successful," he said.
